title: Advance Search
text:
Advance Search 
 Advance 
 Search 
 Documents 
 can be searched independent of the organizational hierarchy, rather 
 at the Enterprise level 
 Multiple 
 Search Parameters can be given from Advanced search, through which 
 transaction tracking is much easier 
 Partial 
 search is also available, i.e. putting a partial string on search 
 box system will filter the data based on the input string available 
 anywhere in that column. 
 For 
 example, in Lead interface of SFA module, different filter options include 
 Id, Mobile Number, Email, Lead Date, Lead Time, Lead Owner, Remarks, Status, 
 Campaign Type, Campaign Sub Type, Campaign Reference, Campaign, Parent 
 Campaign. Account, Origin, Product etc. As shown in the following screen. 
 Whereas in Booking 
 interface of Sales and Customer care module, different filter options 
 include Business Unit, Booking No., Document Date, Unit No., Application 
 No., Customer Name, Hierarchy, Status etc. as shown in the following screen. 
 Advance Search 
 Template 
 Advance search template is used to set entry 
 type wise advance search filter options. 
 Click on the application name 
 Select entry type to filter data based on 
 entry type otherwise find the required entry type in data grid and click 
 on copy icon to copy an existing template. 
 Enter template 
 name. Click 'IsDefault' if the template is used as default template. 
 Select the required 
 filter option(s) and save the template.

title: Transaction in Draft Mode
text:
Transaction in Draft Mode 
 Transactions 
 in Draft Mode 
 Draft mode allows 
 users to temporarily save typed data without storing the data in the actual 
 transactional database. Large transactions can be saved in interim 
 state as Draft mode for future use. User can resume re-entry of transactions 
 from draft mode. 
 Transactions within 
 draft mode are not available for any further subsequent processing. Draft 
 Mode has to be set as ‘ON’ in the interface for Draft mode saving button 
 to be enabled. There is no such setting required for Draft mode enabling. 
 It is enabled by code only. 
 ‘Save As Draft’ 
 is enabled under submit menu. 
 After a document 
 is saved as draft, user can only retrieve it again after making draft 
 mode on in the same interface. 
 Click on the row 
 to open the screen and make further entry or necessary changes. After 
 that user is required to finally submit and save the entry.

title: Report Scheduler
text:
Report Scheduler 
 Report Scheduler 
 Users can schedule 
 reports to be mailed to themselves or other users. User can choose the 
 frequency of emailing reports, and set date and time when the reports 
 will be emailed. 
 To schedule a report, 
 user is required to click on ‘Scheduler’ button and then click on ‘Create 
 Scheduler’. 
 Email Report: Select 
 the option ‘To Me and/or Other’ before adding users or ‘To Me’ to mail 
 the report to the user only. 
 Add/Filter User : 
 Select the user(s) who will receive the report in email by clicking on 
 the user name(s) in left pane. The name(s) will appear in the right pane. 
 To remove the user, user is required to click on the user name in the 
 right pane. 
 Type : 
 There are two types as ‘Run Once’ and ‘Recurring’ 
 If ‘Run Once’ option 
 is chosen then ‘Start Date’ and ‘Start Time’ are to be entered 
 If ‘Recurring’ 
 option is chosen then user is required to set the frequency and schedule 
 the same 
 If ‘Frequency’ 
 is chosen as ‘Daily’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled On’ as 
 ‘Every Day’ or ‘Every Week Day(Mon-Fri)’ 
 If ‘Frequency’ 
 is chosen as ‘Weekly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Day’ 
 in the week 
 If ‘Frequency’ 
 is chosen as ‘Monthly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Date’ 
 in the Month 
 If ‘Frequency’ 
 is chosen as ‘Hourly’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Hour’ 
 If ‘Frequency’ 
 is chosen as ‘Minutes’, then user is required to select ‘Scheduled Minute’

title: Data Import Process
text:
Data Import Process 
 Data Import 
 Process 
 Data can be imported 
 after downloading template excel, fill up with data and save. 
 For example, let 
 us discuss the process of importing account data under Lead Management 
 > Account 
 First, export the 
 template by clicking “Download” button. A file namely account.xlsx will 
 be downloaded. 
 Once the template 
 is filled up, the prescribed template will be ready to import (in this 
 case we have selected the “account.xlsx” template for “Account” import). 
 Related to the 
 data sheet the following measures are to be taken: 
 # 
 there should not be any hyperlink in any of the fields (e.g. Email etc.) 
 # 
 try to import 500 records at a time. 
 Then “Upload” button 
 is to be clicked to get the mentioned template uploaded. 
 The template can be dragged and dropped or 
 the same can be selected from its location and click "U pload 
 file" button . 
 After clicking the “Upload” button it will 
 show the message “Uploaded Successfully”. 
 Then click on Next button to validate the 
 data from the template and click on “Start Validation”. 
 Once the validation is done successfully 
 then it will show the message “Success”. 
 Again the click on Next button to activate 
 “Import Data” tab and click on “Start Import” so that it will start importing. 
 On successful import, it will show the message 
 “Success”. 
 Now click on 
 “Finish” button and the imported data will be populated in the screen.

title: Overview
text:
Overview 
 Help > Setup > Land Bank" />
 Setup 
 Overview 
 The 
 Setup section of the Business Development Module is used to create 
 and maintain master data required for land identification, legal tracking, 
 liaison approvals, and project estimation. 
 These 
 setup configurations help the organization maintain standardized information 
 related to projects, land details, brokers, estimation structures, 
 legal reasons, and government approval processes. 
 All 
 these setups must be configured before using the operational features 
 of the Business Development module. 
 Navigation: Business Development 
 Module > Setup Section (cog icon)

title: Reason Master
text:
Reason Master 
 Help > Setup > Legal" />
 The Legal Setup is used to maintain 
 reasons related to legal cases associated with land or projects. 
 Reason Master 
 Reason Master allows 
 users to specify and manage reasons for why a case is pending. This feature 
 helps in tracking and resolving issues efficiently by providing a clear 
 and organized way to document the reasons for delays. 
 Why Use Reason Master? 
 The primary purpose 
 of the Reason Master is to offer a standardized method for documenting 
 and categorizing the reasons behind pending cases. 
 Use Case Example 
 Consider a scenario where a real estate 
 agent is unable to finalize a property sale because they are waiting for 
 the legal department to complete the title verification process. In this 
 case, the real estate agent would put in the code from the Reason Master 
 for legal verification. 
 By documenting this reason, the team 
 can understand that the delay is due to the legal verification process. 
 This helps in tracking the status of the case and allows the team to follow 
 up with the legal department to expedite the verification. 
 Steps to Use Reason Master 
 Navigate to Business Development> 
 Setup> Legal> Reason Master 
 Fill in the fields as required: 
 Option Type: Choose Reason Master from 
 the dropdown. 
 Code: Enter a unique code for the reason. 
 Description: Enter the reason. 
 Once these details are filled, click 
 on Submit to save the entry.

title: Project Requirement
text:
Project Requirement 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Project 
 Requirement 
 Project Requirement represents the initial 
 requirement raised by a department for a new project. 
 Before identifying land for development, 
 departments specify what type of project they want to develop and what 
 kind of land is required. 
 This interface helps the organization 
 capture those requirements in a structured format. 
 Instructions 
 The 
 header section is the same as other system interfaces and contains 
 basic system information. 
 Users 
 need to define the expected type of project, the preferred location, 
 and the main purpose of purchasing the land. 
 Users 
 should specify the minimum and maximum area of land required, the 
 preferred shape of the land, and the expected FSI. 
 The 
 expected budget for the project and the possible financial variance 
 should be mentioned. 
 Information about road connectivity, infrastructure 
 availability, and surrounding conditions should be provided. 
 Note 
 Most fields 
 in this interface are not mandatory, but it is recommended to provide 
 meaningful details to help the organization identify suitable land.

title: Project Identification
text:
Project Identification 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Project 
 Identification 
 Project Identification is the process 
 of recording a potential project along with the land identified for development. Once 
 a departmental requirement is defined, suitable land can be identified 
 and recorded in this interface. 
 Instructions 
 Enter the proposed or future name of 
 the project and Select the Business Unit responsible for managing 
 and controlling the project. 
 Select the project type from the Setup 
 section such as Commercial, Residential, or Hospital. 
 Choose the project basis such as Self-Financed, 
 Partnership, or Joint Venture. 
 Select the source from which information 
 about the land was obtained. This value comes from the Setup master. 
 Select whether the broker is registered 
 or unregistered. The broker name should be selected from the Supplier 
 Master (Account Head Master). 
 Provide the location details including 
 boundaries and latitude and longitude coordinates. 
 Enter the total plot area of the identified 
 project land. 
 The system validates this value with 
 the plot area entered in Plot Entry and the total project area defined 
 in the Project Budget. 
 Specify the type of agreement such as 
 Barter Agreement or Joint Venture. 
 Attach relevant documents such as location 
 maps, preliminary agreements, or supporting documents.

title: Project Estimation
text:
Project Estimation 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />

 Estimation

 Instructions:

 Users can choose one of the following estimation

 The budget heads are fetched from the Engineering

 These heads can later be linked with the Project 
 Budget in the Engineering module. 
 These heads are created in the Setup section under 
 Estimation Heads for income and expenditure. 
 This estimation method is independent and not linked 
 with the project budget.

title: Overview
text:
Overview 
 Help > Transaction" />
 Overview 
 The Transaction section of the Business 
 Development Module manages the complete lifecycle of land acquisition 
 and related activities. 
 This section helps organizations perform 
 the following activities in a structured manner: 
 Capture departmental requirements for 
 new projects 
 Identify suitable land for development 
 Estimate project profitability 
 Maintain detailed information about 
 plots and landowners 
 Record financial considerations and 
 payments related to land purchase 
 Maintain legal ownership history of 
 the land 
 Register purchased land into the system 
 Track legal cases related to land 
 Manage liaison work and approvals from 
 various authorities 
 Each transaction is connected with the 
 next step, ensuring a complete and traceable process for land acquisition 
 and project planning.

title: Plot
text:
Plot 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Plot 
 Plot Prospect captures the detailed 
 information of individual plots and their respective landowners within 
 the identified project area. This interface helps maintain information 
 about plot numbers, land sellers, and ownership distribution. 
 o Instructions 
 Select the project previously recorded 
 in the Project Identification interface. 
 Provide the plot number, survey number, 
 and Mouja. 
 Enter the seller’s name, address, PAN 
 number, and the plot area occupied by each seller. 
 If multiple occupiers exist, the share 
 of each seller should be clearly defined. 
 The total plot area entered here must 
 match the Total Plot Area defined in Project Identification. 
 Project details will automatically be 
 carried forward from the Project Identification interface. 
 Users can also locate the plot using 
 Google Maps if required. 
 Attach supporting documents such as land records 
 or seller documents. 
 Purpose and Importance 
 The primary purpose of the “Plot” interface 
 is to maintain accurate and comprehensive records of land plots. This 
 is essential for ensuring that all necessary details are captured accurately, 
 which aids in smooth project management and compliance with legal requirements. 
 Use Case Example 
 In the “Green Meadows Residential Project,” 
 the team records land plot details using the Farvision. They validate 
 the total plot area, carry forward relevant information, locate the plot 
 on Google Maps if needed, and attach necessary documents like the sale 
 deed. This ensures accurate and compliant project management. 
 Steps to Import 
 Data for Plot Entry 
 Navigate to Business Development> 
 Land Bank> Plot 
 Click on ‘Advanced Search’ icon and 
 from the Plot dropdown, click on Import. 
 Download the template. 
 Fill in the data in the sheet as follows. 
 Once the sheet is filled, click on ‘Upload 
 Template’ tab and select the sheet which needs to be uploaded. 
 Click on Next to open the ‘Validate 
 Data’ tab. 
 Click on ‘Start Validation’ after which 
 the Status will show Success. The user can also download the result. 
 Click Next to the ‘Import Data’ tab. 
 Click on Start Import to import the 
 data into the system. The Status will show Success. 
 Click on Finish once done and hit the 
 Advanced Search icon to view the imported data. 
 ·

title: Consideration for Plot
text:
Consideration for Plot 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Consideration 
 for Plot 
 · The “Consideration for Plot” interface is designed 
 to assist users in evaluating the financial aspects of purchasing a plot 
 of land. This interface records the financial 
 considerations and expenses associated with acquiring a plot. These 
 expenses may include payments to landowners, brokers, or other charges. 
 Why Is It Important? 
 This interface integrates the price 
 consideration with the purchase value, providing a comprehensive overview 
 of the total cost involved in the transaction while purchasing the plot. 
 Use Case Example 
 Consider a real estate developer looking to purchase 
 a plot of land for development. The developer inputs the plot’s asking 
 price, additional costs (such as taxes, legal fees, and development costs), 
 and any potential discounts or incentives into the interface. The developer 
 can view a detailed breakdown of the total cost. With this information, 
 the investor can decide whether the plot is a viable investment based 
 on their budget and financial goals. 
 S teps 
 to Use Consideration for Plot Interface 
 Instructions 
 Record 
 all expenses incurred for each plot owner and plot. 
 Select 
 the prospect project and filter by plot number and owner name. 
 The 
 broker name will automatically be populated by the system. 
 Select 
 the consideration type and enter the amount for each consideration. 
 Attach 
 supporting documents if necessary. 
 All 
 expenses entered here are validated through the Request for Payment 
 interface. 
 Steps to Import Data for Consideration 
 for Plot 
 Navigate to Business Development > 
 Land Bank > Consideration for Plot. 
 Click on the Advanced Search icon. 
 From the Consideration for Plot dropdown, 
 click on Import. 
 Download the template from this screen. 
 Fill in the sheet, as required, and 
 click on Next to move to the ‘Upload Template’ tab. 
 Here, the user can choose the preferred 
 file and upload it. 
 Click on Next to open the ‘Validate 
 Data’ tab. 
 Click on ‘Start Validation’ and the 
 Status will show as ‘Success’. 
 The user can also download the result. 
 Click on Next to open the ‘Import Data’ 
 tab. 
 Click on ‘Start Import’ after which 
 the Status will show Success. 
 The user can also download the result. 
 Click on Finish once done. 
 Finally, click on Advanced Search icon 
 to view the entries.

title: Registry of Plot
text:
Registry of Plot 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Registry 
 of Plot 
 After completing all related activities such as project 
 identification, plot entry, and payment processing, the final step is 
 land purchase or registration, which is known as the Registry of Plot. 
 Instructions 
 The 
 header contains minimal information except the Subdistrict or Tehsil. 
 Plot 
 Number - Fetched automatically from plot details. 
 Seller 
 Purchaser Deed Number 
 Enter 
 the deed number according to the registration document. 
 Enter 
 the mutation certificate details including tax receipt number or tax 
 amount. 
 Enter 
 the encumbrance certificate or NOC details based on the search results. 
 Important 
 Field – IsInventory -If this checkbox is selected, the system will 
 automatically create an inventory item with the following structure. 
 Land 
 + Plot Number + Subdistrict or Tehsil 
 Item 
 Type 
 FOC 
 Item 
 Value 
 Zero 
 value 
 The 
 system will also automatically create a Stock Adjustment Entry using 
 the area as the quantity. 
 The 
 created land inventory can later be sold through the Sales Module. 
 Once inventory 
 is created, the entry cannot be edited because the item master and stock 
 adjustment entries have already been generated.

title: Title Chain
text:
Title Chain 
 Help > Transaction > Land Bank" />
 Title Chain 
 Title Chain maintains the complete legal 
 ownership history of a plot. This information is important for legal authentication 
 and proof of ownership of assets such as land or buildings. 
 Instructions 
 Select the plot number. All other plot 
 information is automatically fetched from Plot Entry. 
 The area is automatically fetched from 
 plot details but remains editable because ownership may change over 
 time. 
 RS or LR number must be entered manually. 
 Enter the registration date of ownership 
 transfer. 
 Select the title type such as Gift Deed, 
 Sale Deed, Mortgage, or Will. 
 These values come from the Land Bank 
 Setup. 
 Enter the title number and detailed 
 information manually. 
 Enter the owner name according to the 
 mutation certificate. 
 If legal heirs exist, an affidavit must 
 be available. 
 Specify the names of the parties transferring 
 and receiving the ownership as per the deed. 
 Each ownership record should have supporting 
 attachments to maintain the historical chain of ownership.

title: Court Case
text:
Court Case 
 Help > Transaction > Legal" />
 Court Case 
 · This interface is used to maintain the details of 
 legal cases related to land or property. 
 Instructions: 
 The 
 basis value comes directly from the system and does not require setup. 
 If an 
 existing case is reopened or referenced, the previous case reference 
 number can be entered. This field is optional. 
 Select 
 the case type from the predefined system types. 
 Select 
 the legal consultation firm from the Account Head Master under Supplier 
 Type. 
 Closed 
 Status - If the case is closed, the next hearing date and reason are 
 not required. 
 Pending 
 Status - If the case is pending, the following fields become mandatory. 
 Next 
 Hearing Date 
 Reason 
 Next 
 Follow Up Date 
 Follow 
 Up By 
 Workflow 
 The 
 system supports workflow and multi-level approval. 
 Court 
 case data can be imported using an Excel file. 
 Alert 
 emails can be configured for hearing dates and follow-up dates. 
 All 
 follow-up entries will appear in the Follow-Up History section.

title: Court Case Follow Up
text:
Court Case Follow Up 
 Help > Transaction > Legal" />
 Court Case 
 Follow Up 
 · ' C o urt Cases Follow 
 Up' 
 is designed to manage and track follow-ups 
 on pending court cases, ensuring that all necessary actions are taken 
 in a timely manner. 
 Use Case 
 A real estate company manages numerous 
 legal cases related to property disputes, tenant issues, and regulatory 
 compliance. The company uses Farvision with the Court Cases Follow 
 Up feature. 
 For instance, the system prompts the 
 legal team to follow up on a pending case involving a property dispute. 
 The prompt provides details on the specific actions needed, such as submitting 
 additional documents to the court or scheduling a meeting with the involved 
 parties. 
 By following these prompts, the legal 
 team ensures that all necessary steps are taken in a timely manner, maintaining 
 the company’s reputation for thoroughness and reliability. 
 Additionally, the feature maintains 
 a history of all follow-ups, allowing the team to review past actions 
 and decisions. This comprehensive record helps the company manage its 
 legal cases more effectively, providing management with the control and 
 oversight needed to ensure successful outcomes. 
 Steps to Use Court Cases Follow Up Feature 
 Instructions 
 Required Information 
 Next Hearing Date 
 Next Follow Up Date 
 Next Follow Up By 
 Pending Reason (Mandatory) 
 Workflow 
 Multi-level approval workflow can be configured. 
 Follow-up data can be imported using Excel. 
 Follow-up alerts can be configured to notify responsible 
 persons. 
 Once the above details are filled, your 
 screen should look similar to the following. 
 Click on Submit to save the entry.

title: Work Allocation
text:
Work Allocation 
 Help > Transaction > Liason" />
 Work Allocation 
 · This interface is used to assign liaison 
 tasks related to project approvals, permissions, and government sanctions. 
 Navigation: Business Development Module > Liason 
 > Work Allocation 
 · Instructions: 
 Select the Business Unit and transaction 
 date. 
 Choose the level of work. 
 If the work is related to a particular 
 plot, the plot number can be selected. This is optional. 
 The sanction template selection is mandatory. 
 Assign the work to the responsible person, 
 either an internal employee or an external individual. 
 Attach relevant supporting documents 
 if required.

title: Work Done Against Allocation
text:
Work Done Against Allocation 
 Help > Transaction > Liason" />
 Work Done 
 Against Allocation 
 This interface records the 
 progress or completion status of work assigned in Work Allocation. 
 · Instructions: 
 Main Info Tab: 
 o Business Unit: Select from the dropdown (e.g., FACTORY 
 UNIT(KOLKATA)). 
 o Document Type: Choose "LIAISON WORK DONE-(BDWDN)". 
 o Document No: Verify or enter the document number. 
 o Prospect Project: Select the relevant project. 
 o Allocation No: Verify or enter the allocation number 
 (e.g., S1WAL/00001/24-25). 
 o Financial Year: Select the financial year (e.g., 
 01-04-2024 - 31-03-2025). 
 o Document Date: Pick the date (e.g., 26/06/2024). 
 Work Details: 
 o Click "+Add New Row" and fill in the details: 
 o S.No 
 o Allocation No 
 o Assigned To 
 o Sanction Type 
 o Sanction Sub Type 
 o Plot No 
 o Mouja 
 o Status 
 Submit: 
 o Click "Submit" to save. 
 o Click "Cancel" to discard. 
 Additional Tabs 
 o Attachment: Attach documents. 
 o Change History: Review modifications. 
 Once 
 the Allocation number is selected , the Details 
 will automatically be fetched from Work Allocation. If the work is 
 not completed by the due date, the status should remain pending. 
 A 
 new due date must be entered for the pending work.
